findings.before: cut out, stop (an engine, the heart); abandon (an animal); expose (to: jemanden etwas aussetzen); suspend; etwas auszusetzen haben: find fault
findings.after: cut out, stop (an engine, the heart); abandon (an animal); expose (jemanden einer Sache aussetzen); suspend; etwas auszusetzen haben: find fault
findings.why: The pattern is jemanden + Dativ (einer Gefahr, der Sonne aussetzen). 'jemanden etwas' reads as two accusatives and teaches the wrong case.

findings.before: transfer (to another post or class); jemanden versetzen: stand someone up
findings.after: transfer (to another post or place); move up (a school year: versetzt werden); jemanden versetzen: stand someone up
findings.why: In school, versetzt werden means being moved up to the next year, not transferred to another class.

findings.before: The parcel will be delivered tomorrow.
findings.after: The courier will deliver the parcel tomorrow.
findings.why: Keep the active voice and the subject (der Paketbote) of the German sentence.

findings.before: I still have to fold the laundry.
findings.after: I'm just going to fold the laundry.
findings.why: The German has no obligation (no 'muss'); 'noch' here means 'as one more thing'.

findings.before: Concern, tackle: hat angegangen (Wir haben das Problem angegangen). A light going on: ist angegangen.
findings.after: All senses take sein in standard German: Wir sind das Problem angegangen; das Licht ist angegangen. (hat angegangen is regional.)
findings.why: Standard de-DE forms the Perfekt of angehen = tackle with sein (Er ist die Sache falsch angegangen); haben is regional/southern. The note teaches the regional form as the rule. 'Concern' is hardly used in the Perfekt.

findings.before: Ich ziehe Tee dem Kaffee vor.
findings.after: Ich ziehe die Bahn dem Auto vor.
findings.why: Tee without article next to dem Kaffee is uneven; with two count nouns both articles sit naturally and the dative stays visible.

findings.before: I prefer tea to coffee.
findings.after: I prefer the train to the car.
findings.why: Matches the changed example.

findings.before: to be cut, to disappear (jobs, benefits; not formal)
findings.after: to be cut, to no longer apply (jobs, rules, benefits)
findings.why: wegfallen is stylistically neutral and common in official texts (Der Zuschlag fällt weg); 'not formal' wrongly suggests it is colloquial. The new clue also matches the example (rules no longer apply).

findings.before: ent = away from: the name fell away from you.
findings.after: ent = away from: a fee falls away; a name falls away from your memory.
findings.why: The example uses the fee sense; the why only explains the slip-your-mind sense.

findings.before: The doctor prescribes me some medicine.
findings.after: The doctor is prescribing me some medicine.
findings.why: Simple present 'prescribes me' reads as a habitual statement and is stiff; the progressive is the natural English for this scene.

findings.before: I hope I pass the exam!
findings.after: I passed the exam!
findings.why: The German is Perfekt and states a fact (Ich habe die Prüfung bestanden!); the English says something different (a hope about the future).

findings.before: He simply won't admit his mistake.
findings.after: He simply won't see that he's made a mistake.
findings.why: einsehen is to see/accept, not to admit (zugeben); the closer English keeps the meaning line (realise, accept) visible.

findings.before: Please keep two metres apart.
findings.after: Please keep a distance of two metres.
findings.why: Keeps the noun Abstand (distance) visible in the translation.

findings.before: verb |  |
findings.after: verb | SPLITS |
findings.why: blaumachen does split (Ich mache heute blau; hat blaugemacht); the split field is blank and only the note says so. Mark it SPLITS like the other separable verbs.

findings.before: Der Fahrer sagt die nächste Haltestelle durch.
findings.after: Der Zugführer sagt durch, dass der Zug Verspätung hat.
findings.why: For the next stop, natives mostly say 'ansagen'; durchsagen is most typical for a PA message such as a delay, which also matches the clue. New exEn: The guard announces over the PA that the train is delayed.

findings.before: The driver announces the next stop.
findings.after: The guard announces over the PA that the train is delayed.
findings.why: Goes with the changed example.

findings.before: After the annual bill we had to pay a large amount extra.
findings.after: After the final bill we had to make a large extra payment.
findings.why: The German does not say 'annual'; Abrechnung is the final statement or bill, and the English should keep the noun 'payment'.

findings.before: to clear (a backlog, a to-do list) task by task
findings.after: to work through (a to-do list) item by item
findings.why: 'einen Rückstand aufarbeiten' is the standard collocation for a backlog (the why of aufarbeiten says so too); dropping 'backlog' keeps the clue off aufarbeiten, which is on the same B2 board.

findings.before: It takes four weeks to deal with your application.
findings.after: Processing your application takes four weeks.
findings.why: Keeps a noun for the noun being taught; 'Bearbeitung eines Antrags' = processing in official English.

findings.before: Our cat went missing three days ago.
findings.after: Our cat ran away three days ago.
findings.why: entlaufen = ran away (escaped); 'went missing' is vermisst/verschwunden. The literal sense matches the meaning line better.

findings.before: The money is not distributed fairly.
findings.after: The distribution of the money is not fair.
findings.why: Mirrors the noun the card teaches; still natural English.

findings.before: das: an + ge + bot; nouns built with ge- are mostly das (das Gebot, das Verbot).
findings.after: das: an + ge + bot; nouns built with ge- are mostly das (das Gebot, das Aufgebot).
findings.why: das Verbot is ver + bot, not a ge- noun; citing it as an example of the ge- rule teaches a false analysis.

findings.before: Learn it as a word: ver- (old for-) + bieten (bid, order) is English for-bid.
findings.after: ver- matches English for-, bieten matches bid: verbieten is literally for-bid.
findings.why: 'Learn it as a word' is the grade-O formula but the grade is M and the why then derives it; drop the contradiction.

findings.before: Der neue Laden unterbietet alle Preise in der Stadt.
findings.after: Der neue Laden unterbietet die Preise der Konkurrenz.
findings.exEn: The new shop undercuts its competitors' prices.
findings.why: One undercuts rivals or their prices; 'alle Preise in der Stadt' is slightly odd as a collocation.

findings.before: The new shop undercuts every price in town.
findings.after: The new shop undercuts its competitors' prices.
findings.why: Goes with the changed example.

findings.before: be- makes fragen act on a person: you put questions to someone.
findings.after: be- makes it systematic: you put a series of questions to someone (a witness, people in a survey).
findings.why: fragen already takes the person as object (jemanden fragen), so the stated contrast is misleading.

findings.before: She is taking over management of the project.
findings.after: She is taking over the management of the project.
findings.why: More natural English with the article.

findings.before: C1
findings.after: B2
findings.why: Common in official and job contexts (Kenntnisse nachweisen); C1 is high next to der Nachweis B1 and nachweisbar B2.
